roleContext.jobDescription: A developer-tools company hosts source repositories for software teams and offers full-text code search across them. The search infrastructure team runs the indexing workers, the query service and the search clusters on Kubernetes. The engineer will tune query latency, keep the indexing pipeline healthy during large repository imports, write capacity plans and join the team's weekday on-call. Latency work is judged on percentiles from the query service's own metrics, compared over fixed windows before and after a change with similar traffic.

requirements.text: Operates Elasticsearch or OpenSearch clusters running on Kubernetes.
Improves query latency and shows the result as percentiles over fixed windows before and after the change.
Keeps a high-volume indexing pipeline reliable, including back-pressure and retry handling.
Writes capacity plans for search clusters covering compute, memory and storage.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Backend Engineer, Search Infrastructure

## Experience

- Ran four OpenSearch clusters on Kubernetes at Quillmark, a code-hosting company, handling node-pool upgrades and shard rebalancing during maintenance windows.
- Reduced p99 latency of the code-search query service from 2.4 seconds to 0.9 seconds, comparing the two weeks before with the two weeks after the switch to per-repository routing in May 2023.
- Added back-pressure to the indexing workers so that large repository imports paused queue consumption instead of overloading the clusters, with retries capped at five attempts.
- Took part in the weekday on-call rotation for the search stack and wrote two post-incident reviews.
- Drafted the 2024 storage forecast for the search clusters from twelve months of index-growth data; the infrastructure lead reviewed it before the hardware order.

## Work samples

- Work sample: the latency write-up for per-repository routing, with the query service's p50, p95 and p99 tables for 1 to 14 May 2023 (p99 2.4 s) and 22 May to 4 June 2023 (p99 0.9 s), the routing design diagram and a check showing query volume within 5% across the two windows.
